record.paper_title: Beam energy scan theory: Status and open questions
record.original_question: Does QCD matter, in the region probed by low- and intermediate-energy heavy-ion collisions, undergo a first-order phase transition between quark-gluon-plasma matter and hadron-gas matter, and if so is there a critical endpoint associated with that transition?

evidence.quote: Is there a first order phase transition between the quark-gluon plasma and the hadron gas and a critical endpoint?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider quantum chromodynamics (QCD), the SU(3) gauge theory of quarks and gluons, at finite temperature T and finite baryon chemical potential μ_B. The grand-canonical partition function on the (T, μ_B) plane defines a thermodynamic phase structure with two known regimes: (i) a high-temperature, deconfined quark–gluon plasma phase, and (ii) a low-temperature, confined hadron-gas phase. At μ_B = 0 lattice QCD establishes that the change between these regimes is a smooth analytic crossover. Determine the following about the phase diagram in the region of moderate to large μ_B accessible to low- and intermediate-energy heavy-ion collisions:

(a) Does there exist a curve T_c(μ_B) in the (T, μ_B) plane along which the free energy is non-analytic and across which the system undergoes a genuine first-order phase transition (i.e., a discontinuity in the baryon density and/or energy density) between the quark–gluon plasma phase and the hadron-gas phase?

(b) If such a first-order transition line exists, does it terminate at a critical endpoint (T_E, μ_B^E) with 0 < T_E and 0 < μ_B^E < ∞, at which the transition becomes second order in the 3D Ising universality class, and the crossover region begins?

Provide either a proof of existence together with the location (or rigorous bounds on the location) of the critical endpoint, or a proof that no such first-order line and endpoint exist in this region.
artifact.category_tag: QCD phase diagram and critical endpoint
artifact.status_search_result: The existence of a first-order deconfinement/chiral transition line at finite baryon chemical potential and an associated QCD critical endpoint remains an open problem. Lattice QCD is hindered by the sign problem at μ_B > 0, and experimental searches (RHIC Beam Energy Scan I and II, NA61/SHINE) have not yet produced conclusive evidence as of 2026. Recent reviews continue to list it as unresolved.

status_evidence.title: The QCD phase diagram and Beam Energy Scan physics: a theory overview
status_evidence.snippet: The existence and location of a possible critical endpoint in the QCD phase diagram remains one of the central open questions, being addressed by the BES program.
status_evidence.claim: Existence/location of QCD CEP still open as of recent reviews.

status_evidence.title: Lattice QCD at non-zero density and the sign problem
status_evidence.snippet: Direct lattice simulations at finite μ_B are obstructed by the sign problem; current results are consistent with crossover and do not establish a first-order line.
status_evidence.claim: Lattice cannot yet decide whether a first-order line exists at large μ_B.
